_README: Ops that the reachability audit reports as having no caller outside their own package.
'intentional' â€” an op that is SUPPOSED to have no external caller. Every entry
needs a real reason; an empty one fails the test. This is the escape hatch for
ops driven by a background worker, a dynamic dispatch the text scan can't read,
or a deliberately manual operator action.
'backlog' â€” the debt baseline captured on the audit's first run (2026-08-01).
These are NOT approved. They are frozen so that new unreachable code fails CI
immediately while the existing pile is worked down. The test ratchets both ways:
adding an unlisted unreachable op fails, and wiring a backlog op up ALSO fails
until it's deleted from this list â€” so the number can only go down.
Do not add to 'backlog'. Wire the op up, or justify it in 'intentional'.

intentional.publishing.render: Synchronous render, superseded by the enqueueRender/renderQueuedJob queue path which the worker tick drives. Kept because MontageRenderer's tests exercise it directly and a blocking render is still useful for one-off debugging.
intentional.backup.restore: Deliberately operator-only. Restoring a snapshot overwrites live state, so it must not be reachable from a route or an autonomous cycle â€” an accidental call is unrecoverable.
intentional.setup.runAutonomous: First-boot provisioning, run once by hand via `pnpm setup`. Wiring it to a route would let a stray request re-provision a live instance.
intentional.email.send: Deliberately NOT wired. @atlas/sender is the single path email leaves ATLAS by, and its suppression list and CAN-SPAM checks only mean anything if there is no second route around them. Exposing email.send would be exactly that route. The email plugin is kept for its READ side (email.check, used by gigfinder.checkWins to spot client replies).

backlog._note: Found by the audit's first run. Untriaged â€” presence here is a record of debt, not a judgement that it is correct.
